title: Building a Production-Grade Profile Service (Spring MVC)
audience: Senior backend engineers responsible for customer data platforms.
summary: Design the system context, data contracts, and Spring MVC implementation for a resilient customer profile service, then harden it for production readiness.

prerequisites.title: Professional Java Experience
prerequisites.description: Comfort with Java 17, dependency injection, and building REST APIs in Spring.

prerequisites.title: Operational Awareness
prerequisites.description: Familiarity with distributed tracing, metrics, and structured logging in cloud environments.

prerequisites.title: Database Fundamentals
prerequisites.description: Understanding of relational data modeling, indexing strategies, and transactional boundaries.

learningModel.framing: Start with the architecture: map which systems publish profile mutations today, which consumers depend on the data, and the failure modes that force rework or incidents.
learningModel.coreActivity: Iteratively design and implement the service, alternating between architecture checkpoints (context, container, component views) and hands-on Spring MVC development with tests.
learningModel.feedback: Use architecture decision records, pairing reviews, and telemetry-driven tests to validate each iteration before promoting it to the next environment.
learningModel.transfer: Apply the same architecture-first approach and delivery guardrails to other customer data surfaces or shared platform APIs.

lessonPlan.overview: Follow five facilitated blocks that move from architecture framing to deployment readiness. Each block ends with a tangible artifact or demo.

segments.title: Architecture Context Briefing
segments.focus: Align on business capabilities, stakeholders, and the bounded context for the profile service.
activities: Review stakeholder map and current-state integration points.
Draft a system-context diagram capturing upstream and downstream systems.
Identify cross-functional quality attributes (latency, compliance, resiliency).
deliverables: System-context diagram annotated with actors and protocols.
Architecture decision record (ADR) summarizing scope and constraints.

segments.title: Domain Modeling & Contract Design
segments.focus: Translate business capabilities into aggregates, contracts, and data flows.
activities: Model the profile aggregate, read models, and event contracts in a whiteboard session.
Define REST and async contracts (JSON schema, Avro, or Protobuf) for create/update/search operations.
Design migration strategy for legacy profile identifiers and partial updates.
deliverables: Domain glossary and ERD for canonical profile storage.
Contract catalog describing REST endpoints and message topics.

segments.title: Service Skeleton & Observability
segments.focus: Stand up the Spring MVC skeleton, persistence layer, and baseline telemetry.
activities: Generate controller, service, and repository layers using Spring Initializr and company standards.
Implement DTO validation, optimistic locking, and persistence mappings to PostgreSQL.
Instrument OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and structured logs for critical paths.
deliverables: Passing integration tests (Testcontainers) for CRUD flows.
Dashboard mock-up demonstrating golden signals for the service.

segments.title: Resilience & Data Synchronization
segments.focus: Protect dependencies and synchronize data to secondary stores without data loss.
activities: Introduce resilience4j circuit breakers, retries, and rate limiting for downstream search indexes.
Model outbox patterns or change data capture for profile replication.
Run chaos drills that simulate downstream outages and verify recovery procedures.
deliverables: Sequence diagram describing failure handling and recovery flows.
Synthetic check plan verifying replication lag and error budgets.

segments.title: Production Readiness Review
segments.focus: Harden deployment workflows, governance artifacts, and support playbooks.
activities: Align CI/CD stages with automated smoke, contract, and load tests.
Establish rollout strategies (feature flags, shadow traffic, canaries).
Document on-call handoff, alert routing, and runbook expectations.
deliverables: Release checklist covering migration, rollback, and communication steps.
Support playbook outlining escalation paths and observability dashboards.

competencyPillars.name: Architecture & Domain Modeling
competencyPillars.description: Translate customer identity requirements into a robust domain model that cleanly separates write, read, and search responsibilities.
outcomes: Document service boundaries, upstream dependencies, and API contracts.
Design persistence schemas that accommodate eventual search and analytics use cases.
Capture domain events to keep downstream projections eventually consistent.
examples: Decompose the monolithic profile database into command and query models with separate lifecycle policies.
Map how profile merges propagate to marketing automation and analytics consumers without double counting.

competencyPillars.name: Spring MVC Implementation
competencyPillars.description: Build a layered Spring MVC application that exposes secure CRUD operations, optimistic locking, and request validation.
outcomes: Scaffold controllers, services, and repositories with clear separation of concerns.
Implement DTO validation and sanitize untrusted input at the edge.
Introduce integration tests with Testcontainers to cover real database interactions.
examples: Demonstrate how controller advice normalizes error payloads for partner teams.
Showcase optimistic locking preventing lost updates when customer data specialists edit the same record.

competencyPillars.name: Resilience & Observability
competencyPillars.description: Harden the service for production by adding circuit breakers, backpressure, and first-class telemetry.
outcomes: Apply resilience4j patterns to protect downstream dependencies.
Emit OpenTelemetry spans, metrics, and structured logs for critical interactions.
Define golden signals and dashboards to support on-call readiness.
examples: Use synthetic profile mutations to validate SLO burn alerts before launch.
Capture correlation IDs across Kafka consumers, the profile service, and the search index updater.

competencyPillars.name: Delivery Workflow
competencyPillars.description: Plan how the service moves from commit to production with confidence, including automated quality gates and phased rollout.
outcomes: Configure continuous delivery pipelines with smoke, integration, and contract tests.
Implement feature flags and shadow traffic to derisk deployment.
Run load testing and chaos experiments before enabling general availability.
examples: Stage blue/green deployments with automated rollback when replication lag exceeds thresholds.
Shadow 5% of identity updates through the new service before cutting traffic.

competencyPillars.name: Stakeholder Enablement
competencyPillars.description: Ensure partner teams can integrate the profile service and support their own downstream use cases.
outcomes: Publish API docs, onboarding guides, and SLA expectations.
Co-design synthetic events and sandbox data for client teams.
Establish escalation paths, alert routing, and response playbooks.
examples: Create onboarding runbooks for experimentation teams consuming identity signals.
Provide customer support with scripted diagnostics for common profile sync issues.

architectureGuide.context: Anchor your implementation in three complementary architecture views, capturing both runtime interactions and operational trade-offs.

views.name: System Context
views.focus: Show how the profile service mediates between identity providers, consent management, and downstream personalization engines.
decisions: Expose REST APIs for synchronous customer updates while emitting domain events for asynchronous consumers.
Treat the profile service as the system of record for mutable profile attributes while search and analytics act as projections.
tradeOffs: Balancing synchronous writes for consistency with async replication latency for analytics.
Managing regulatory obligations (GDPR/CCPA) across multiple downstream storage systems.

views.name: Container View
views.focus: Detail the deployable units: Spring MVC service, PostgreSQL cluster, Kafka topics, search indexer, and observability stack.
decisions: Deploy the API behind an ingress controller with WAF and mutual TLS for partner integrations.
Use a managed PostgreSQL cluster with read replicas to support high-volume read workloads.
Adopt Kafka for change propagation so additional projections can subscribe without coupling.
tradeOffs: Higher operational overhead for Kafka offset management versus simplified webhook integrations.
Running read replicas introduces replication lag that the API must communicate to clients.

views.name: Component View
views.focus: Break the service into API, application, domain, and infrastructure layers plus supporting modules.
decisions: Separate command handlers from query resolvers to support divergent read/write scaling paths.
Implement an outbox pattern within the persistence layer to guarantee event delivery to Kafka.
Encapsulate observability concerns in cross-cutting interceptors to avoid duplicating boilerplate.
tradeOffs: Higher upfront complexity for CQRS compared to a single repository layer.
Outbox pattern adds storage overhead but prevents dual-write inconsistencies.

referenceImplementations.label: Spring PetClinic Microservices
referenceImplementations.summary: Demonstrates production-grade Spring Boot services with service discovery, circuit breakers, and centralized config.

referenceImplementations.label: Event Sourcing & CQRS with Spring
referenceImplementations.summary: Showcases outbox and event-driven patterns that map to the profile replication requirements.

referenceImplementations.label: OpenTelemetry Java Instrumentation
referenceImplementations.summary: Provides reference instrumentation, exporters, and deployment guidance for consistent telemetry.

integrationProject.overview: Build a greenfield customer profile service that ingests profile updates from upstream systems, exposes a REST API, and synchronizes to downstream search indices.

iterations.title: Iteration 1: Domain & Service Skeleton
iterations.objective: Deliver the architecture artifacts and a functional Spring MVC skeleton ready for CRUD workloads.
tasks: Finalize system-context, container, and component views plus supporting ADRs.
Implement core create/read/update flows with DTO validation and optimistic locking backed by PostgreSQL.
Ship integration tests that exercise the HTTP surface, domain layer, and persistence using Testcontainers.

iterations.title: Iteration 2: Observability & Resilience
iterations.objective: Instrument the service and protect dependencies so failures are transparent and recoverable.
tasks: Add OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs; publish dashboards for latency, throughput, and error budgets.
Introduce resilience4j policies (circuit breakers, retries, bulkheads) for downstream search index updates.
Document failure scenarios and attach runbooks to each alert with clear mitigation steps.

iterations.title: Iteration 3: Data Synchronization & Delivery
iterations.objective: Guarantee downstream consistency and production-readiness for launch.
tasks: Implement an outbox or CDC pipeline to publish profile change events to Kafka and feed the search indexer.
Configure CI/CD with automated schema migrations, smoke tests, and staged rollouts (shadow traffic + canary).
Run load and chaos tests, capture findings, and update the release checklist accordingly.

reflection.description: Use these prompts during a retro or personal reflection session once the project is complete.
prompts: Which architecture decision delivered the most leverage for downstream teams?
How did observability insights change the rollout or support plan?
Where did resilience patterns absorb real failure scenarios during testing?
What should be templatized for other services adopting similar customer data flows?
